title: Sample research note
description: This is a fictional note used to preview the research section in development. It compares three made-up ways to keep a sourdough starter alive while travelling, and how well each one holds up after a week away.

versions.summary:
## Findings revised
- Dried starters recover in 2 to 3 feedings, not 3 to 4. The 2026 survey update measured this across 120 dried samples ([survey](https://example.org/survey-2025)).

## New since last edit
- 2026-09-02: the Example Baking Lab moved its drying guide to a new page ([guide](https://example.com/baking-lab/drying-v2)).

## What changed
- Freezing: "least predictable" -> "least predictable, about one in five fail to revive", with a new row in the methods table.

## Re-verified, unchanged
- Refrigeration recovery times and the spoilage signs.

## Not verified
- none

## Findings revised
- none

## New since last edit
- 2026-10-12: a revival procedure from the updated drying guide, now its own section ([guide](https://example.com/baking-lab/drying-v2)).

## What changed
- Removed the claim that an acetone smell fades after one feeding. No current source supports it.

## Re-verified, unchanged
- The main finding, the methods table and the spoilage signs.
